title: The big pack can cost more
hook: A larger pack looks like a bargain. What happens per kilogram?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Normalize different pack masses to cost per kilogram.

misconception: The largest pack always has the lowest unit price.
objective: Normalize different pack masses to cost per kilogram.

claims.text: A costs €3 for 500g. B costs €6 for 900g. Scaled model; prices fictional; same product.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Large-price=6€, A=6€/kg and B=6.667€/kg. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",3,0.5]; B=["/","x",0.9]; x denotes Large-price. At x=6, A=6, B=6.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Dividing price by kilograms puts both packs on the same denominator. Pack size alone does not determine unit price; the receipt and quantity must travel together.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",3,0.5]; B=["/","x",0.9]; x denotes Large-price. At x=6, A=6, B=6.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Fictional packs of the same product: 400g for €2, or 1kg for €6. Which costs less per kilogram? Correct: The 400g pack. €2 ÷ 0.4kg = €5/kg, below €6/kg: divide price by mass, because pack size alone does not set the unit price.

claims.text: A unit price expresses cost per stated quantity; comparable unit-price labels use consistent units of measure.
claims.source: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/1181e2025/NIST.SP.1181e2025.html NIST SP 1181-2025, Definitions / Unit Pricing and E-Commerce. Opened 2026-10-13. recall.question: Fictional packs of the same product: 400g for €2, or 1kg for €6. Which costs less per kilogram?
